category_description: State Pension rates and age, pension tax allowances and workplace pension minimums.
subcategory_description: How much the State Pension pays and when you can claim it.
subject_intro: The full weekly State Pension for 2026/27 under the new and old schemes, and the National Insurance years needed to qualify.
subject_meta_description: The full new State Pension is £241.30 a week in 2026/27 and the basic State Pension £184.90, with 35 qualifying years needed for the full new rate.
label: Full new State Pension (weekly)
context: For people who reached State Pension age on or after 6 April 2016. Your own amount depends on your National Insurance record.

label: Qualifying years for the full new State Pension
context: People who were contracted out before 2016 usually need more.

label: Minimum qualifying years for any new State Pension
Full basic State Pension (weekly)
context: For men born before 6 April 1951 and women born before 6 April 1953.

subject_intro: The State Pension age is rising from 66 to 67 in monthly steps between April 2026 and 2028, depending on your date of birth.
subject_meta_title: State Pension Age: The Rise From 66 to 67
subject_meta_description: State Pension age is 66 for anyone born before 6 April 1960, rising in monthly steps to 67 for anyone born on or after 6 March 1961.
label: State Pension age if born before 6 April 1960
State Pension age if born on or after 6 March 1961
context: People born between 6 April 1960 and 5 March 1961 reach State Pension age between 66 and 67, one month later for each month of birth. A further rise to 68 is currently scheduled for 2044 to 2046.

subcategory_description: How much can go into pensions each year with tax relief, and how much can be taken out tax-free.
subject_name: Pension Annual Allowance and Lump Sum Limits
subject_intro: The yearly limit on tax-relieved pension saving, how it shrinks for high earners and after drawing a pension, and the caps on tax-free lump sums.
subject_meta_title: Pension Annual Allowance and Tax-Free Lump Sum 2026/27
subject_meta_description: Pension allowances for 2026/27: £60,000 annual allowance, £10,000 money purchase annual allowance and £268,275 lump sum allowance.
label: Annual allowance
context: The most that can be saved into pensions each tax year, by you and your employer combined, before a tax charge. Unused allowance from the previous three years can usually be carried forward.

label: Money purchase annual allowance
context: Applies instead once you've flexibly taken money from a defined contribution pension.

label: Annual allowance starts to taper above (adjusted income)
context: Falls by £1 for every £2 of adjusted income above this, if threshold income is also above £200,000.

label: Taper only applies if threshold income exceeds
Lump sum allowance
context: The most that can be taken as tax-free lump sums over your lifetime, unless you hold a protected allowance.

label: Lump sum and death benefit allowance
context: The overall cap on tax-free lump sums in life and certain lump sums paid on death before 75.

subcategory_description: Automatic enrolment rules and the minimum contributions employers and employees must pay.
subject_intro: When employers must automatically enrol staff into a workplace pension, and the minimum that has to be paid in.
subject_meta_description: Workplace pension auto-enrolment for 2026/27: £10,000 earnings trigger, 8% minimum contribution including 3% from the employer, on earnings from £6,240 to £50,270.
label: Auto-enrolment earnings trigger
context: Workers aged 22 to State Pension age earning more than this must be enrolled automatically.

label: Qualifying earnings: lower limit
context: Minimum contributions are usually worked out on earnings between the lower and upper limits, not the whole salary.

label: Minimum total contribution
context: Includes the employer's share and the employee's contribution with tax relief.
